NEW DELHI: Union minister Kiren Rijiju on Saturday posed five questions to the Congress, a day before the opposition INDIA bloc's rally at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan to seek the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls."I challenge the Congress party to answer these basic questions," he posted on X.Rijiju first question was how the Congress managed to win just 44 seats in the 2014 Lok Sabha elections, despite the polls being conducted by an Election Commission whose members were appointed under the then Congress-led UPA government.Pointing out that Kumar was not the CEC during the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, having been appointed to the EC only ahead of the polls and elevated to the top post in 2025, the minister questioned how the Congress still lost, marking its third consecutive Lok Sabha election defeat.The Congress-led opposition has repeatedly accused Kumar of manipulating elections in favour of the BJP.Meanwhile, Rijiju further asked whether all sitting Congress chief ministers would resign and whether the party would apologise for forming governments between 2014 and 2026, if it had won elections despite alleged manipulation in the BJP's favour.His next questions focused on the SIR, with Rijiju asking whether illegal immigrants, deceased individuals and people who had relocated should be removed from electoral rolls, and whether the eight previous revision exercises were also "illegal."The current protests follow a report published by The Indian Express in September, which stated that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had objected at least 14 times to decisions they claimed were taken without their knowledge, including those concerning the SIR.Responding to the report, the EC said that disagreements were common in multi-member institutions and that all decisions were ultimately taken unanimously.Decisions in the poll panel are taken either by consensus or by a 2-1 majority.
Article Summary: Union minister Kiren Rijiju on Saturday posed five questions to the Congress. He was a day before the opposition INDIA bloc's rally at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan. The opposition is seeking the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar.

Article Title: 'Let's walk together': Rahul Gandhi invites people to march ahead of INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan
Article Text:
Delhi Police says no permission sought on INDIA bloc march to Ramlila Ground

NEW DELHI: Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi on Saturday invited people to join a march in the national capital on Sunday before reaching Ramlila Maidan, where the INDIA bloc is scheduled to hold a mega rally on November 1.However, Delhi Police sources told news agency ANI that no permission had been sought for the proposed march from Connaught Place.In a post on X, Rahul shared the route and schedule of the march, saying, "See you tomorrow, let's walk together."According to his post, the march will begin at the Minto Road junction near Connaught Place at noon on Sunday. Participants will proceed towards Ajmeri Gate before concluding at Ramlila Maidan.Responding to Rahul's announcement, Delhi Police sources told ANI that no application had been received seeking permission for a march from Connaught Place. They added that MPs and political leaders were free to travel in their private vehicles to the Constitution Club, Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge's residence or any other location of their choice.The sources also pointed out that Jantar Mantar, traditionally a designated venue for protests in the capital, has been de-notified as a protest site.They said Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), which restricts assemblies and gatherings, is currently in force across the New Delhi area, including the vicinity of the Election Commission.Police said elaborate security arrangements would be made at Ramlila Maidan for Sunday's rally. Personnel from multiple Delhi Police districts, including the Central District, will be deployed along with paramilitary forces.Meanwhile, INDIA bloc leaders are scheduled to hold a public programme on the proposed impeachment of chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar on Saturday at 3.30 pm at 10, Rajaji Marg, the residence of Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge.The programme was postponed from Friday due to rain in the national capital. Announcing the decision, Gandhi said the leaders had agreed to reschedule it to avoid inconvenience to senior members.Speaking to reporters in Delhi on Friday, Rahul said, "By consensus, we have decided to postpone today's program (public impeachment programme against CEC) to tomorrow at the same time because of rain. We felt that it would be uncomfortable for seniors to sit in the rain, and we will hold the same program tomorrow."He also urged political parties, civil society members, journalists and other citizens to join the INDIA bloc's November 1 march to Ramlila Maidan."The day after, we have a march to Ramlila Maidan. All the opposition, everybody who wants to come: political, non-political, social, service people, civil society people, journalists. Both the programs are about the demolition of Indian democracy by Narendra Modi, by Amit Shah, by Gyanesh Kumar and his crew in the Election Commission," he said.Raebareli MP further alleged that Union home minister Amit Shah was trying to prevent people from travelling to Delhi to attend the rally."The home minister is trying his best to stop people from coming into Delhi, trying to ensure that our party members, common people who want to come from UP, Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Haryana, Telangana, Punjab, are being stopped. And they're trying their best," former Congress chief said.
Article Summary: Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi invited people to join a march in the national capital on Sunday. Delhi Police sources told news agency ANI that no permission had been sought for the proposed march from Connaught Place. Jantar Mantar, traditionally a designated venue for protests in the capital, has been de-notified as a protest site.

Article Title: Surrender before December 1: Supreme Court cancels bail of expelled JD(U) leader Anant Singh in Dularchand Yadav murder case
Article Text:
Anant Singh

Murder case and legal proceedings

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Friday cancelled the bail granted to expelled JD(U) MLA Anant Singh in the murder case of Dularchand Yadav and directed him to surrender before the authorities on or before December 1, 2026.A bench of Justices MM Sundresh and PV Varale observed that the Patna High Court had erred in granting Singh bail without adequately considering the nature of the offence and his criminal antecedents. The top court suspended the High Court's order and cancelled the relief granted to Singh.The verdict comes days after the ruling Janata Dal (United) expelled Singh and his wife, former MLA Neelam Devi, from the party for six years over alleged anti-party activities.Singh had openly defied the party leadership by campaigning for Jan Suraaj candidate Anuj Kumar Singh instead of the JD(U)'s official nominee, Neeraj Kumar, in the Patna Graduates' constituency Legislative Council elections. He also reportedly made remarks against senior party leaders and questioned the functioning of the party leadership.Following the expulsion, the Bihar government stripped Neelam Devi of her position on the State-Level Programme Implementation Committee, withdrawing her minister of state rank and entitlement to an official bungalow.On October 26, the state government's Building Construction Department issued an eviction notice directing her to vacate her official residence at 1, Mall Road in Patna.The JD(U) has also approached Bihar Assembly Speaker Prem Kumar seeking Singh's disqualification under the anti-defection law. The petition was filed under the direction of party state president Umesh Singh Kushwaha.Dularchand Yadav, a regional strongman, was murdered on October 30, 2025, during a clash in Mokama Tal while campaigning for the Bihar Assembly elections was underway. Yadav was backing Jan Suraaj candidate Piyush Priyadarshi when his supporters allegedly clashed with Singh's convoy.According to the FIR registered at Ghoswari police station, Singh and his aides allegedly dragged Yadav out of his vehicle, shot him in the leg, assaulted him and ran over him with an SUV.Singh, however, claimed that the incident was part of a political conspiracy orchestrated by a rival politician. He alleged that Jan Suraaj supporters had attacked his convoy first.Bihar Police arrested Singh on November 1, 2025, and lodged him in Beur Central Jail. Despite being in custody, he contested and won the Mokama Assembly seat on a JD(U) ticket.The Patna high court granted him bail on March 19, 2026, following which he was released from prison. The bail order was subsequently challenged in the Supreme Court in October by Neeraj Kumar, the grandson of Dularchand Yadav.
Article Summary: Supreme Court cancels bail granted to expelled JD(U) MLA Anant Singh in the murder case of Dularchand Yadav. Justices MM Sundresh and PV Varale observed that the Patna High Court had erred in granting Singh bail without adequately considering the nature of the offence and his criminal antecedents.

NEW DELHI: The Bharatiya Janata Party is planning to launch a counter-protest in Delhi against the Congress-led INDIA bloc's rally against voter irregularities at Ramlila Maidan on November 1, news agency ANI reported.According to the report, around 5,000 people are expected to participate in the march in the Hari Nagar area of the national capital.Members of the Sikh community, especially victims of the 1984 anti-Sikh riots and their family members, are also likely to join the BJP's march as the party is gearing up for the upcoing Punjab assembly elections.Their participation is likely to bring the issue of the 1984 riots into focus, with the BJP seeking to highlight the alleged role of Congress leaders in the violence.This comes as the BJP has questioned Rahul Gandhi over holding the 'Delhi Chalo' march on November 1, which is also the anniversary of the 1984 anti-Sikh riots in Delhi following the assassination of former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi.Several senior BJP leaders from the Sikh community, along with other prominent party leaders, are expected to join the march. This issue is being raised very seriously by our party. November 1 is a day that holds deep emotional significance for the Sikh community, as they remember the 1984 massacre with profound sorrow," Prasad had said during a BJP press conference.Meanwhile, INDIA bloc constituents are also gearing up for a show of strength at the opposition's rally on November 1. Article Title: 'Did we use pellet guns?' Kapil Sibal hits back at Kiren Rijiju over remarks on protests under Congress rule
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Former Union minister Kapil Sibal on Friday referred to the alleged use of pellet guns against student protesters by security forces in Delhi, saying that the Congress government had "never used" pellet guns or resorted to lathi-charge against demonstrators, unlike the current BJP-led government.His remarks came a day after Union minister Kiren Rijiju shared a video from 2011 featuring Sibal, who was then a Union minister, addressing a press conference on the India Against Corruption movement, which had challenged the Congress-led UPA government.In the video, Sibal, who is no longer associated with the Congress, had said, “Right to protest is not the right to protest at the place of your choice.”Sharing the clip, Rijiju called Sibal a “Dimagi Naxal” and remarkeed that the senior advocate had exposed the Congress's “secrets” and “thoroughly torn Rahul Gandhi to shreds”, referring to the Congress MP and Lok Sabha leader of the opposition.In a subsequent post, Rijiju questioned whether any "new laws" governing protests had been introduced since 2014, when the BJP came to power.Hitting back at Rijiju at a press conference in Delhi, Sibal first questioned the former law minister’s legal experience.“I wish I could have seen him somewhere in court -- in my 50-odd years at the courts, at least I have not seen him in the corridors of the court,” he remarked, accusing the BJP MP of criticising others without understanding the facts.Rejecting the claim that the UPA government had opposed protests, he challenged the minister to cite instances when the Congress-led government had used pellet guns or resorted to lathi-charge against demonstrators.“We never ensured that people don’t protest. In fact, on one occasion… in a Cabinet meeting this issue was discussed, and my colleagues said, ‘Look, this is a right under the Constitution, you cannot interfere with this right, this is a constitutional right,’” Sibal added.He also highlighted the role of protests in India’s Independence movement, arguing that they could lead to another form of independence.Criticising Rijiju’s handling of parliamentary affairs, Sibal remarked, “As far as Parliamentary Affairs is concerned, we know how he (Rijiju) runs Parliament. That is his expertise: to ensure that the voice of the opposition is not heard for which he should get a medal of some kind.”“They don't allow us to raise the issues we want to raise. They don't allow us to protest. They pass bills without a discussion. They are unconcerned with parliamentary procedures. The manner in which Parliament was functioning was unprecedented in India’s history,” he added.Sibal further stated that the Congress would allow Rijiju to speak if he found himself in the opposition in the future: “Rijiju ji, please remember: history repeats itself.”Clashes broke out between student protesters and security forces in Delhi on July 20 as demonstrators marched towards Parliament, demanding the resignation of then Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan over the NEET-UG paper controversy. The Delhi Police and Rapid Action Force were accused of using pellet guns to disperse the protesters and stop their march.Pradhan resigned on July 25, bringing the protests to an end.
Article Summary: Kapil Sibal hits back at Kiren Rijiju for calling him a 'Dimagi Naxal' Sibal says the Congress government had "never used" pellet guns or resorted to lathi- charge against demonstrators, unlike the current BJP-led government.

Article Title: Form 7 row: Supreme Court directs EC to probe bulk applications during Uttar Pradesh SIR
Article Text:
SC directed EC to probe alleged irregularities involving bulk submissions of Form 7s during UP SIR (Representative image)

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Friday directed the Election Commission (EC) to examine allegations of irregularities in the bulk submission of Form 7 applications during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in Uttar Pradesh and take necessary corrective measures.A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana asked the petitioners to submit a note to the EC detailing the "unresolved irregularities" they had flagged."The irregularities which have been brought to the notice of the court shall be submitted to senior counsel appearing for the Election Commission of India by way of a note. On receipt thereof, let the Election Commission examine the factual aspects, thereafter take necessary corrective steps and file a compliance report," the bench said, according to PTI.The Supreme Court was hearing petitions filed by Congress MP Tanuj Punia and others challenging the SIR exercise in Uttar Pradesh. More than 13 crore electors were included in the final electoral roll ahead of the assembly elections scheduled in the state early next year.The opposition has alleged that over 2.04 crore names were removed from the electoral rolls during the revision.During the hearing, counsel for the petitioners alleged that 32 Form 7 applications had been submitted in one constituency to target members of a particular community.Senior advocate DS Naidu, appearing for the EC, acknowledged that bulk Form 7 applications had been filed but said no action had been taken on them."We found that bulk Form 7 applications had been submitted. Our officers checked and cross-checked them. They were false, and we have not acted upon them," Naidu told the court.Following the submissions, the CJI-led bench directed the EC to examine the matter.
Article Summary: SC directed EC to probe alleged irregularities involving bulk submissions of Form 7s during UP SIR. More than 13 crore electors were included in the final electoral roll ahead of the assembly elections scheduled in the state early next year. Opposition has alleged that over 2.04 crore names were removed from the electoral rolls during the revision.

Article Title: Judge named accused in son’s fatal Mercedes crash gets interim protection from arrest
Article Text:
Jayabalakrishnan, who ran a roadside eatery, was heading home after closing the shop when the accident occurred at 2.20 am on Sunday. Both vehicles were travelling towards Kalamassery.





KOCHI: The Kerala high court on Thursday granted interim protection from arrest to the additional district judge whose 17-year-old son allegedly drove a Mercedes-Benz that hit a two-wheeler in Kochi, killing the rider.Justice Kauser Edappagath passed the order on an anticipatory bail plea filed by the judge, who is posted at a Motor Accident Claims Tribunal in Irinjalakuda, Thrissur district.“The police shall not arrest the applicant until further orders. However, he shall appear before the investigating officer today at 1pm and if necessary as and when called for. The interrogation of the applicant shall be done in accordance with the guidelines laid down by the Supreme Court,” the court ordered.Senior advocate P Vijaya Bhanu, appearing for the judge, told the court that his client had appeared before the police on Wednesday and was interrogated for more than four hours. Another notice directing him to appear before the police had since been issued.According to Bar and Bench, questioning the need for further interrogation and custodial questioning, the court remarked, “What was the need to interrogate him for four hours and now for further interrogation? Why is his arrest required? He is a judicial officer.He will co-operate with the investigation.”Counsel representing the victim’s legal heirs opposed the plea, alleging that the judge had tampered with evidence after being informed of the accident.The court said it had to proceed strictly in accordance with the law and granted interim protection from arrest. It also asked the prosecutor to provide the state’s response to the plea.The judge was named as an accused in the FIR registered after the October 25 crash in Cheranalloor, Kochi, in which his minor son allegedly drove the car that hit a two-wheeler, killing Jayabalakrishnan.In his anticipatory bail plea, the judge claimed he had no knowledge that the vehicle had been taken from the premises. He said he learnt of the accident after receiving a phone call while asleep.The plea also argued that Section 105 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, which deals with culpable homicide not amounting to murder, requires knowledge that the act is likely to cause death.Meanwhile, the victim’s family has complained to the Kerala high court chief justice seeking an inquiry into the judicial officer’s conduct. According to Bar & Bench, the High Court’s Administrative Committee held a preliminary meeting on October 27 and decided to await further material from the investigating agency before taking any action against the judge.
Article Summary: The Kerala high court on Thursday granted interim protection from arrest to the additional district judge. His 17-year-old son allegedly drove a Mercedes-Benz that hit a two-wheeler in Kochi, killing the rider. Justice Kauser Edappagath passed the order on an anticipatory bail plea filed by the judge, who is posted at a Motor Accident Claims Tribunal.

Article Title: BJP now left with just one graduate constituency seat in Maharashtra
Article Text:
Maharashtra's recent MLC elections have shown a decline in BJP's influence in graduate constituencies (File pic)





MUMBAI: With MVA winning three of five MLC seats, all graduate constituencies, BJP's hold over its once-strongholds has weakened sharply. The party now has just one MLC from the seven graduate constituencies in the legislative council.The council has 78 seats, of which seven each are reserved for graduates' and teachers' constituencies. NCP (SP) winning Pune and Chhatrapati Sambhaji Nagar and Congress taking Nagpur, leave BJP with only one graduate constituency MLC: Niranjan Davkhare from Konkan, who joined BJP from NCP in 2018.Graduate constituencies, particularly Nagpur, Pune and Mumbai, were once BJP bastions. Party stalwarts such as Nitin Gadkari, Prakash Javadekar, Chandrakant Patil and late Gangadharo Fadnavis, father of chief minister Devendra Fadnavis, have won these elections."Graduates' constituency MLC polls are important because they provide direct legislative representation to the educated population and serve as a key indicator of the political mood among urban, middle-class professionals. BJP has lost Mumbai, Pune and Nagpur, the state's three most important centres for educated professionals and cultural activity. This is a setback," a political observer said."Earlier, Congress was BJP's principal rival in most constituencies. The BJP and RSS machinery took the initiative in voter registration, enrolling graduates on a large scale. Over 10 years the picture has changed. BJP's dominance among graduates has been broken, and the opposition has gained ground across the six constituencies it does not hold. Konkan is the exception, where BJP's representative is an NCP import," he said.Mumbai, too, has moved away from BJP. Madhu Deolekar was the party's graduate constituency MLC immediately before Shiv Sena's Pramod Navalkar won the seat. It has remained a Sena (UBT) stronghold since.
Article Summary: BJP's hold over its once-strongholds has weakened sharply. The party now has just one MLC from the seven graduate constituencies in the legislative council. The council has 78 seats, of which seven each are reserved for graduates' and teachers' constituencies.

Article Title: Water in petrol: Sambhajinagar pump owner faces FIR 5 years after complaints

TOI





Five years after complaints of petrol mixed with water, Cidco police have registered a case against the owner of a petrol pump on Jalgaon Road in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar.The FIR was registered on the complaint of district supply officer Bharti Wakode under sections 3 and 7 of the Essential Commodities Act. The FIR mentions the findings of the inspection conducted on Nov 16, 2021, the number of customers who had complained at the time, and the laboratory report dated Dec 26, 2022, which confirmed traces of water in petrol.The criminal action follows an order passed by the Bombay high court in a writ petition filed by activist Manish Narwade.“The incident dates back to Nov 16, 2021. On that day, 40 to 50 customers who had filled petrol at the pump complained that water was present in the petrol supplied to them. Following the complaints, an inspection was carried out at the pump and samples were collected,” Narwade said.As per the complaint, samples were drawn from three nozzles at the fuel station and sent to the laboratory for testing. The laboratory report was received on Dec 26, 2022. The report allegedly confirmed the presence of water traces in the samples collected from the three nozzles. However, no offence was registered by authorities, following which Narwade took legal recourse.“Despite the laboratory confirmation in Dec 2022, the FIR was not registered at that time. A writ petition was subsequently filed before the Bombay high court’s Aurangabad bench seeking directions for action based on the inspection and lab report,” Narwade said.Pursuant to the high court order, the district supply office submitted a complaint to Cidco police, based on which the FIR was registered on Oct 23.“The case is significant because it relates to adulteration of fuel with water, which causes damage to vehicles and loss to consumers. The five-year gap between the complaint, the lab report and the registration of the FIR has also brought the issue of delayed action in adulteration cases into focus,” Narwade said.The management of the petrol pump on Jalgaon Road refused to comment when contacted by
Article Summary: Cidco police have registered a case against the owner of a petrol pump on Jalgaon Road in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar. The criminal action follows an order passed by the Bombay high court in a writ petition filed by activist Manish Narwade.

Article Title: Rs 1 lakh bribe trap: Navi Mumbai ACB catches circle officer, talathi and woman assistant
Article Text:
The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite, Jaihind Birsha Koli (49) and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36).





NAVI MUMBAI: The Navi Mumbai Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) has arrested two revenue officials and a woman assistant for allegedly accepting a Rs 1 lakh bribe from a villager in Chirner, Uran taluka, to register the names of his relatives in the 7/12 extract of a land record.The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite (52), circle officer at Koproli in Uran taluka; Jaihind Birsha Koli (49), talathi; and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36), an assistant to the revenue officials.Dharmaraj Sonake, deputy superintendent of police, Navi Mumbai ACB, said the complainant had applied to register the names of the heirs of his deceased sister in the 7/12 extract of their land in Chirner.The land was jointly owned by the complainant's maternal uncle, aunt, brother and sister. The complainant had also applied for deletion of his deceased brother's name and submitted the request to circle officer Mohite and talathi Koli. However, the two officials allegedly demanded Rs 1 lakh from him to process the work.Dy SP Sonake said, "After verification of the complaint on Monday, when it was confirmed that the revenue officers Mohite and Koli had told the complainant to hand over the bribe amount to the accused woman assistant Monika Patil, a trap was laid on Tuesday around 2 pm. After the woman assistant Monika Patil accepted the demanded bribe of Rs 1 lakh from the complainant and handed it over to circle officer Keshav Mohite, both were caught red-handed and arrested. While, the acccused Talathi Jaihind Koli who was involved in the bribe demand was taken into custody from Dronagiri."
Article Summary: The Navi Mumbai Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) has arrested two revenue officials and a woman assistant for allegedly accepting a Rs 1 lakh bribe. The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite (52), circle officer at Koproli in Uran taluka; Jaihind Birsha Koli (49), talathi; and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36)

Article Title: Man in Mahindra Thar with duplicate plate molests woman, knocks down another in Kharghar
Article Text:
30-year-old man was apprehended for allegedly molesting a woman and injuring another in Navi Mumbai.





NAVI MUMBAI: A 30-year-old man wearing a mask and driving a red Thar SUV with a duplicate registration number plate was apprehended by the Crime Branch Unit-3 team within 10 hours on Thursday evening.He had allegedly molested a 26-year-old woman walking on the street in Kharghar, around 400metres from Pethpada metro station, on September 30 night and, an hour later, severely injured a 22-year-old woman by knocking her down in Belpada, Sector 3, Kharghar.Acting on a complaint by the woman allegedly molested by the Thar SUV driver, Kharghar police registered an FIR under BNS section 74 for the offence of assault or criminal force against a woman with the intent to outrage her modesty.While, as per the complaint by the injured woman Shrawani Dandekar, a resident of sector 3, Belpada, an FIR under relevant BNS sections and Motor Vehicle Act was registered against the Thar SUV driver for rash and negligent driving causing hurt.The detained aaccused identified as Ali alias Talib Ahsan Nakhvi, a resident of sector 50, Seawoods, Nerul was handed over to Kharghar police for further legal action.Previously, in January 2021, he was arrested by Nerul police in the FIR registered against him for alleged kidnapping, sexual harassment and molestation of a woman.Sanjay Joshi, senior inspector of Kharghar said, "The accused Nakhvi has been detained and subsequently it will be decided whether to arrest him or serve with a notice under Bharatiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) for cooperating in police investigating."Audumbar Patil, senior inspector of crime branch unit-3 said, "After an FIR for molestation was registered at Kharghar police station by the victim woman, a resident of sector 34, Kharghar. As per the orders of higher authority, our team started a parallel probe. From the CCTV camera surveillance near the crime scene, we obtained the red Thar SUV's registration number, which was of Vashi RTO passing.""When verified, the registration number was found to be that of a Maruti WagonR car. As the accused had used a duplicate registration number plate, we scrutinized as many as 62 Thar SUVs registered with various Regional Transport Offices (RTOs). Subsequently, we obtained the registration number of a red Thar SUV that was registered with Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar RTO," Patil added.SPI Patil further informed, "The SUV was registered in the name of Ali alias Talib Ahsan Nakhvi, a resident of Devaki Apartment in sector-50, Seawoods. From his mobile number registered with the RTO, his location was tracked.""He was apprehended from Bonkode village, Koparkhairane on Thursday late evening. Upon thorough interrogation, he confessed that he had inappropriately touched the woman pedestrian near Pethpada metro station while he drove his Thar SUV and sped away. He even confessed to have injured a woman pedestrian by hitting her his SUV while driving in Belpada area," he said.
Article Summary: A 30-year-old man wearing a mask and driving a red Thar SUV with a duplicate registration number plate was apprehended by the Crime Branch Unit-3 team on Thursday evening. He had allegedly molested a woman walking on the street in Kharghar, around 400metres from Pethpada metro station, on September 30 night. An hour later, he severely injured a woman by knocking her down in Belpada, Sector 3, KharGHar.

Article Title: 2 women escape from RPF lockup in Navi Mumbai; 1 held after 6 hours, cop suspended
Article Text:
The women removed their sarees, tied one end to the generator on the balcony and climbed down before escaping. (AI image)





NAVI MUMBAI: In a major security lapse at Belapur Railway Protection Force (RPF), two women arrested for allegedly attempting to steal overhead electric wires from the Juinagar railway godown escaped from the lockup after midnight on September 28.One of them was apprehended around six hours later, while the other remains at large.The woman constable on night duty has been suspended and a departmental inquiry has been initiated against her.As per the FIR registered by RPF sub-inspector Milap Parte (52) at Panvel GRP, a case was registered on September 24 under Section 3(a) of the Railway Property (Unauthorized Possession) Act, 1966, Amendment 2012, at Belapur railway police station.The case was based on a written memo submitted by RPF personnel Ravikant Gade regarding the theft of overhead electric wires from the godown at Juinagar railway station on September 21.During the probe, a trap was laid on September 26 and around 1pm, two women were found loitering suspiciously near the Juinagar godown with the alleged intention of committing theft.They were taken into custody and identified as Rupali Kailas Kurhade (30), from Jalna, and Shalibai Ashok Pawar (49), from Bhiwandi.They were arrested after an FIR was registered for attempted theft and produced before a CSMT court, which remanded them to police custody till September 30. They were lodged in the lockup at Belapur RPF police station.Day-shift woman constable Rakhi Malaiya was assigned guard duty at the lockup, after which woman head constable Pooja Bagre was on night duty.Around 2am on September 28, when Bagre had gone to the toilet, the two women allegedly managed to open the lock by inserting their hands through the iron bars of the lockup and jerking it. Police suspect the lock may not have been secured properly.The women then reached the balcony at the rear end of the police station. They removed their sarees, tied one end to the generator on the balcony and climbed down before escaping.The incident was captured on CCTV footage. PSI Parte learnt about the escape after waking up at home around 6.30am and finding several missed calls from head constable Bagre and ASI Rajiv Parsan.Sunil Nila, chief spokesperson of Central Railway, said, "One accused woman Rupali Kurhade was apprehended from near Nerul railway station around 8.45 am. The other accused Shalibai Pawar is still absconding."
Article Summary: The women removed their sarees, tied one end to the generator on the balcony and climbed down before escaping. One of them was apprehended around six hours later, while the other remains at large. The woman constable on night duty has been suspended and a departmental inquiry has been initiated.

Article Title: TMC suspends fire chief over immersion ghats lapses
Article Text:
Thane municipal corporation





THANE: The Thane municipal corporation (TMC) on Friday suspended its acting chief fire officer (CFO) over alleged negligence in providing adequate safety equipment at idol immersion ghats on Oct 20. Action has also been taken against two other officials, while show-cause notices have been served on two junior staff, it is learnt.The suspension order is issued by additional municipal commissioner-1, Prashant Rode, holds Jhalke responsible for lapses in carrying out his duties. The order states that he has been suspended under the Maharashtra Civil Services (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, 1979. Jhalke, who is the fire officer and in-charge of Balkum fire station, has been handling the additional charge of CFO for the last several years."Certain safety arrangements at Datta Mandir Ghat and Ahilyadevi Ghat at Masunda Lake were allegedly found to be inadequate, with a particular shortfall in life jackets and other essential safety equipment. The shortcomings were apparently pointed out to deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde who also expressed concern at the alleged negligence," said a civic official.Officials said that during the suspension period, Jhalke will be required to comply with the prescribed conditions and cannot take up other employment or engage in business without the requisite permission.
Article Summary: Thane municipal corporation suspends acting chief fire officer (CFO) over alleged negligence. Action also taken against two other officials, while show- cause notices have been served on two junior staff. Safety arrangements at Datta Mandir Ghat and Ahilyadevi Ghat at Masunda Lake allegedly found to be inadequate.

Article Title: Sealed Thane flat in Iqbal Kaskar-Dawood Ibrahim money laundering case breached; ED reclaims property, files FIR
Article Text:
Thane flat linked to Iqbal Kaskar’s extortion case targeted for occupation





MUMBAI: Enforcement Directorate (ED) filed an FIR for trespassing and attempting to occupy a flat in Thane which was attached in a money laundering case it investigated against Iqbal Kaskar and his Pakistan-based gangster brother Dawood Ibrahim The flat was attached in the case in 2022, in the money laundering case linked to extortion by Iqbal Kaskar and others.The flat was in ED’s possession and it had put its seal on the lock. Kaskar had acquired the flat through extortion and threat in 2015 and got it registered in the name of his associate Mumtaz Azaz Sheikh, alias Raju.Recently, the ED learnt that certain persons entered the flat after removing its possession notice, claiming ownership of the flat.Since the money laundering case is pending in the court, the ED informed the court about it, repossessed the flat and filed a police case last week.
Article Summary: Enforcement Directorate (ED) filed an FIR for trespassing and attempting to occupy a flat in Thane. The flat was attached in a money laundering case it investigated against Iqbal Kaskar and his Pakistan-based gangster brother Dawood Ibrahim. The ED repossessed the flat and filed a police case last week.

Article Title: Constable held for demanding Rs5,000 from truck driver near Chandni Chowk after occupants of another truck passing by intervened
Article Text:
Representative image

Pune:





A police constable attached to the Pune police headquarters allegedly demanded Rs5000 from the driver of a container truck and threatened to seize the vehicle if the driver didn’t pay at the Katraj-Dehu Road bypass near Chandni Chowk on Thursday.Warje Malwadi police on Thursday arrested the constable based on a complaint by the 23-year-old truck driver from Bhiwandi in Thane district.An officer from Warje Malwadi police said the driver was on his way to Bengaluru for a delivery when a hatchback car forced him to stop his container truck near Chandni Chowk around 11.30am. A man dressed in khaki got out of the car, asked the driver to produce the truck documents and his driving licence, and demanded Rs 5,000 after checking the papers. The accused threatened to seize the vehicle and prevent the driver from proceeding if he failed to pay.“Meanwhile, another truck stopped there after its occupants noticed the confrontation. Two men from the vehicle intervened after allegedly seeing the constable demanding money from the driver. Around the same time, our patrolling vehicle reached the spot and took the constable into custody,” the officer said.The police have registered a case against the constable under sections 308 ( extortion ) and 126 (wrongful restraint) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).
Article Summary: Warje Malwadi police on Thursday arrested the constable based on a complaint by the 23-year-old truck driver. The driver was on his way to Bengaluru for a delivery when a hatchback car forced him to stop his container truck near Chandni Chowk.

Article Title: Two held for robbing dry fruit trader of Rs4 lakh with the help of three accomplishes in Pimpri
Article Text:
Representative image

Pune:





Two men allegedly robbed a dry fruit trader of Rs4 lakh with the help of three accomplices while the trader was returning home after shutting shop on Thursday night in Pimpri.Pimpri police on Friday arrested the two men while the three accomplices are being searched for.Senior police inspector Rupali Bobade of Pimpri police said that around 10.40 pm on Thursday, the two arrested men and their three accomplices forced the trader, who was riding home on his two-wheeler, to stop. “They threatened him with a sharp weapon. The trader had kept his shop’s daily earning in the scooter’s boot. One of the accused took away the trader’s scooter and fled.”“We registered a case of robbery and have picked up the two main accused from Kalewadi. We have also recovered the trader’s scooter and another scooter allegedly used by the accused,” Bobade said.
Article Summary: Pimpri police on Friday arrested the two men while the three accomplices are being searched for. The trader had kept his shop's daily earning in the scooter’s boot. One of the accused took away the trader's scooter and fled.

Article Title: Malegaon civic chief among 3 arrested for Rs 80,000 bribe demand
Article Text:
Nashik:





The anti-corruption bureau on Thursday arrested Malegaon’s municipal commissioner Ravindra Jadhav, his personal assistant Nilesh Patil and accountant Harish Dimber for allegedly demanding a bribe of Rs 80,000 to clear payments for civic works. The arrests came just days before Jadhav’s retirement on Oct 31.According to the anti-corruption bureau (ACB), the trio demanded 4% commission from the complainant who had been authorised by two contractors to realise the payments from the civic body.“The complainant had submitted a formal complaint on July 9, 2026, stating that authorisation letters were issued for two contractors who executed municipal works for the Malegaon Municipal Corporation. To disburse the bills directly to the contractors’ bank accounts via RTGS, the public servants demanded a 4% bribe on each of the two bills, totalling Rs 80,000. Following the verification of the demand, a trap was laid by the ACB on Thursday and the three were arrested,” said deputy superintendent of police (ACB) Swatee Pawar.Police said Patil repeatedly demanded the bribe on July 10 and 13 and assured the complainant that he would consult the commissioner.The ACB further alleged that Jadhav himself reiterated the demand on July 24 and indicated that the money could be collected after the contractors received their payments. Officials said Dimber allegedly supported and facilitated the demand during subsequent interactions.Based on the complaint and verification of the demand, the ACB laid a trap on Thursday. Jadhav and Patil were arrested in Igatpuri while travelling towards Mumbai, while Dimber was held in Malegaon. A case has been registered at Malegaon Killa police station under the Prevention of Corruption Act. Jadhav has been booked under section 7, while Patil and Dimber face charges under sections 7 and 12.ACB teams also carried out searches at the residences and premises linked to the accused and are examining documents that could strengthen the investigation.Malegaon’s deputy mayor Shaan-e-Hind Nihal Ahmed called for administrative reforms in the civic body. “While the law will decide the fate in this case, residents of Malegaon, however, hope that govt will now depute IAS officers as commissioners, as they are better administrators and are dedicated for the development of the local bodies,” Ahmed said.
Article Summary: Malegaon’s municipal commissioner Ravindra Jadhav, his personal assistant Nilesh Patil and accountant Harish Dimber were arrested on Thursday. The trio demanded 4% commission from the complainant who had been authorised by two contractors to realise the payments from the civic body.

Article Title: Denied cash for liquor by wife, man murders 6-yr-old son by throwing him into well
Article Text:
women body

Villupuram:





A 40-year-old man was arrested on Friday for murdering his six-year-old son by throwing him into a well after his wife denied him cash for consuming liquor at a village near Gingee in Villupuram district. Police said that K Selvaraj, a daily wage labourer from Nallan Pillai Pettral village, and his wife S Devi, 35, have four daughters aged between eight and 14 years and a six-year-old son.Selvaraj allegedly picked up a quarrel with his wife on Thursday night and threatened to kill the children if she refused to give him cash to buy alcohol. As the quarrel spilt over into Friday morning, Selvaraj murdered his son, Sanjay , by throwing him into a farm well behind a govt primary health centre around 9am, said police.Villagers alerted the Sathyamangalam police, and a team arrived with fire and rescue services personnel from Keelpennathur. As the well was brimming with water due to recent rains, rescue personnel deployed pumps to drain the well before recovering Sanjay’s body three hours later. The body was sent to Gingee govt hospital for postmortem. Police registered a case and arrested Selvaraj. Probe is on.
Article Summary: K Selvaraj, a daily wage labourer from Nallan Pillai Pettral village, and his wife S Devi, 35, have four daughters aged between eight and 14 years and a six- year-old son. He allegedly picked up a quarrel with his wife on Thursday night and threatened to kill the children if she refused to give him cash to buy alcohol.

Article Title: 864 bottles of liquor seized from house near Erode; man arrested
Article Text: ERODE: Police seized 864 bottles of Indian made foreign liquor (IMFL) from a house near Mylambadi in Erode district in the early hours of Thursday and arrested a man.Acting on a tip-off that bottles of liquor had been illegally stored for unauthorised sale, the Bhavani police conducted a raid at the house of K Govindaraj, 28, of Ammapalayam. They found 864 bottles of IMFL stocked in the house for illegal sale.Police registered a case and arrested Govindaraj. He was remanded in judicial custody.They launched a search for Sekar alias Ammasai, 34, and Sridhar, 38, who have links with the illegal liquor operation.
Article Summary: Police seized 864 bottles of Indian made foreign liquor (IMFL) from a house near Mylambadi in Erode district. Acting on a tip-off that bottles of liquor had been illegally stored for unauthorised sale, the Bhavani police conducted a raid.

Article Title: Stalin gives zero marks to TVK govt, EPS gives “less than zero”
Article Text:
DMK president M K Stalin





Madurai/Trichy: DMK president M K Stalin on Friday gave chief minister C Joseph Vijay’s five-month-old govt zero marks, while AIADMK general secretary Edappadi K Palaniswami said he would give less than zero marks.Speaking to reporters after paying homage to Muthuramalinga Thevar at Pasumpon in Ramanathapuram district, Stalin alleged that rising crime, skyrocketing prices and political vendetta against opposition leaders were the achievements of the govt.On police cases against former DMK ministers, he said, “We will face it legally. We will prove in court that we are not offenders.” Stalin said DMK would not be deterred by such cases as the party has faced Emergency as well as tough laws like MISA, TADA and POTA.Stalin said disillusionment with the administration had spread even among TVK voters, accusing Vijay of treating CM’s post like a nine-to-five job.He cited sexual assaults, missing girls and the escape of 17 inmates from Theni sub-jail as examples of an alleged breakdown in law and order.Earlier in the day he posted a video message on X, Stalin said Vijay should discharge duties of the chief minister before trying to play the role of “thaai maaman” or “annan.” He alleged that TVK administration neither has administrative efficiency on its own nor the sense to listen and act on advice given by others. He said Saturday’s DMK women’s wing demonstrations across district headquarters would be a “wake-up call” for the govt.Speaking to reporters at Trichy airport, EPS said that law and order in Tamil Nadu has plunged to abysmal levels. “People have doubts whether they will be able to return home safely everyday. I will give only ‘minus zero’ marks to the TVK govt’s performance,” he said.On AIADMK’s stand in the five assembly by-elections, he said, “The decision will be taken after the election is announced.”When reporters asked whether those who were expelled from the AIADMK would be taken back into the party, EPS, “Those who were expelled would remain expelled.”
Article Summary: DMK president M K Stalin on Friday gave chief minister C Joseph Vijay’s five- month-old govt zero marks. Stalin alleged that rising crime, skyrocketing prices and political vendetta against opposition leaders were the achievements of the govt.

Article Title: Seeman open to DMK-AIADMK support in Ambasamudram bypoll
Article Text:
Seeman open to DMK-AIADMK support in Ambasamudram bypoll

Madurai:





NTK chief Seeman on Friday expressed willingness to accept support from arch-rivals DMK and AIADMK in the Ambasamudram bypoll, raising the prospect of opposition parties uniting against the ruling TVK.Speaking after paying homage to Muthuramalinga Thevar at Pasumpon, Seeman used a biryani analogy when asked whether he would accept their backing. “If a hungry man is offered biryani, would he refuse it? We will accept it,” he said.Seeman maintained that electoral support should not be mistaken for an alliance. “Political criticism is one thing; ideological positions are another,” he said, referring to his attacks on Stalin and AIADMK head Edappadi K Palaniswami . He clarified that neither party had decided to field him as a common candidate and accused TVK functionaries of fuelling the speculation.Seeman, who announced his candidature on Thursday, urged voters to give him an opportunity to demonstrate his performance in the assembly. Promising to transform Ambasamudram into a model constituency, he challenged Vijay’s TVK to a direct contest with NTK to establish their respective political strength.His remarks gained significance after DMK president M K Stalin , questioned at Pasumpon about supporting Seeman, stopped short of ruling out the possibility.“Let the election date be announced first. We will decide on that afterwards,” Stalin said.The vacancy arose after AIADMK legislator Esakki Subaya, who won the 2026 assembly election by 10,245 votes over Congress candidate VP Durai, resigned and joined TVK. TVK’s S Rajagopal finished third with 53,611 votes, while NTK’s V Sivasankaran secured 14,906 votes.
Article Summary: NTK chief Seeman open to DMK-AIADMK support in Ambasamudram bypoll. Seeman used a biryani analogy when asked whether he would accept their backing. DMK president M K Stalin stopped short of ruling out the possibility.

Article Title: PE teacher suspended after national flag turns upside down at state sports meet in Salem
Article Text: SALEM: A physical education teacher has been suspended following a protocol lapse during the opening ceremony of the state-level 67th Republic Day Athletics Competitions held at the Mahatma Gandhi Sports Ground here on Wednesday.The incident occurred when the state transport minister A Vijay Tamilan Parthiban was hoisting the national flag, and a snag in the rope caused the flag to fly upside down. The event was organized by the state school education department.Taking immediate note of the negligence during the flag-hoisting ceremony, Salem chief educational officer A Ellappan issued an order placing physical education teacher John Jamindar who had supervised the flag hoisting area.
Article Summary: A physical education teacher has been suspended following a protocol lapse during the opening ceremony of the state-level 67th Republic Day Athletics Competitions. The incident occurred when the state transport minister A Vijay Tamilan Parthiban was hoisting the national flag. A snag in the rope caused the flag to fly upside down.

Article Title: Two history-sheeters who escaped from Attayampatti police station nabbed
Article Text: SALEM: Two history-sheeters, who escaped from the Attayampatti police station in Salem district on Tuesday, were nabbed in the early hours of Wednesday.The duo, identified as Santhosh Kumar and Prabhu, are residents of Kandarkula Manickam near Attayampatti. According to police, Santhosh Kumar and Prabhu were brought to the Attayampatti police station on Tuesday morning in connection with robbery and theft cases and questioned by sub-inspector Krishnan and other police personnel. Subsequently, cases were registered against them.Later, police were making arrangements to produce them before a court in the evening. “However, taking advantage of an opportunity, Santhosh Kumar and Prabhu managed to escape from the police station,” said a police officer.Special police teams were formed to trace them. After an intensive search operation, the duo were tracked down and arrested from near Tiruchengode around 3am on Wednesday.They were brought back to the Attayampatti police station for further inquiry. Later, they were lodged in the Salem Central Prison under judicial custody.
Article Summary: The duo, identified as Santhosh Kumar and Prabhu, are residents of Kandarkula Manickam near Attayampatti. They were brought to the police station on Tuesday morning in connection with robbery and theft cases and questioned by sub- inspector Krishnan and other police personnel.

Article Title: Police arrest drug case accused on the run for two years from Kullu
Article Text:
Kochi

:





The prime accused in a major drug case has been arrested nearly two years after going into hiding. Nedumbassery Police arrested Ragesh, alias Jumanji, 32, of Thalappilly, Thrissur, from Kullu in Himachal Pradesh.On June 27, 2024, the police seized 316g of MDMA, two LSD stamps and 420g of ganja from a car at Athani. The drugs were allegedly being transported from Bengaluru.In connection with the case, the police had earlier arrested Asad, 38, of Chalakkal, Aluva, and Harikrishnan, 28, of Tirurangadi, Malappuram. The vehicle was also taken into custody.The police said that Ragesh had allegedly provided financial assistance for purchasing the drugs. After learning that the others had been arrested, he fled to Kullu.He had been living in hiding as a tourist guide at a resort located more than 20km uphill from the Kullu base camp.The investigation team disguised themselves as tourists and stayed in the area before taking Ragesh into custody.The team was led by district police chief K S Sudarshan and included DSP Baiju Paulose, inspector B K Arun, sub-inspectors Arun Raj and Rony Augustine, assistant sub-inspector M V Binu, and civil police officer Sajash.The accused was produced before court and remanded in custody.
Article Summary: Ragesh, alias Jumanji, 32, of Thalappilly, Thrissur, from Kullu in Himachal Pradesh. Police seized 316g of MDMA, two LSD stamps and 420g of ganja from a car at Athani.
